newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran gives new, lower earthquake death toll.
newsitem.headline: Iran gives new, lower earthquake death toll.

text.p: Iran on Tuesday issued lower numbers for casualties in the major earthquake which rocked its eastern region, saying 1,560 people had been killed and 2,810 injured.
A senior Interior Ministry official in Qaen near the epicentre of Saturday's 7.1 force quake said the figures were accurate up to Tuesday morning.
There was no explanation for earlier official reports that about 2,400 had died and 6,000 were injured.

Rasul Zargar, chief of the Interior Ministry's headquarters in charge of natural disasters, said 10,500 tents, 25,000 blankets and large quantities of food and clothing had been distributed among survivors.
The total damage inflicted on the region would be released next week, he added.
Iranian officials have put a cost of $100 million on damage caused by the earthquake, the second major jolt to strike Iran in less than three months.

About 1,000 people were killed and 2,600 injured in February when a 5.5 Richter magnitude quake hit Iran's northwest. The same region was hit again on Monday by a 4.8 force quake which caused no casualties or damage.
Another earthquake struck the Qaen region late on Monday with a force of 4.8. There was no word of casualties.
